names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 1 iunie, «Sfântul Iustin Martirul și Filosoful».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 1 Ιουνίου, «Άγιος Ιουστίνος ο Απολογητής και φιλόσοφος», with the rank word and the two epithets left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 1. јун ст. ст., „Свети мученик Јустин Философ“ — Свети is not a rank and мученик is the `martyr` this corpus puts in `types`, so both are stripped and the bare form keeps the epithet Философ, which is the one thing in the heading that tells him from the Јустин of the company below. THE FULLER FORM IS DELIBERATE AND MEASURED: `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for both «Јустин Философ» and «Јустин» today, but a bare «Јустин» here beside the bare «Јустин» the company below needs would be two folders on one string and a fold with nothing to tell them apart. One form, the fullest, as §6 requires. AND A FOLD IS NAMED IN ADVANCE: `justin-popovich` is kept on this same menologion day and his Serbian form is «Јустин Поповић», so when a later reader writes it the two will stand on adjacent strings and must be told apart by their centuries.

Name page 1152 heads him «Иустин Философ, Великий, Римский, мч.» — four words of name and epithet and then the grade. The stored form keeps the two the day line itself uses, «Иустина Философа» in the genitive; «Великий» and «Римский» are further epithets the day line does not print and are recorded here instead of stored, because «Римский» is also the whole of what distinguishes the OTHER Justin of this same line, whose form is «Иустин Римский». Measured with the gate's own fold before writing: 'иустин философ' has no other holder.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 1 июня ст. ст. — «Мчч. Иустина Философа и другого Иустина и с ними Харитона , Хариты , Евелписта , Иеракса , Пеона и Валериана (166).»

attestations.note: The day's first entry of seven, and it is one line naming EIGHT people: «Мчч. Иустина Философа и другого Иустина и с ними Харитона , Хариты , Евелписта , Иеракса , Пеона и Валериана (166).» — Justin the Philosopher, «другого Иустина», the other Justin, and then Chariton, Charito, Euelpistus, Hierax, Paion and Valerian. Eight name links stand under it, one for each, and all eight already had folders in this corpus. The year the line gives the whole company at once is 166, and the life it links, life1210, says «пострадали одновременно со святым Иустином Философом , в 166 году»; this folder's recorded 163 comes from the Охридски пролог and was NOT moved — the two sources disagree by three years and neither is preferred here. life1210's own title names the company differently from the day line: «Мученики Иустин, Харитон, Евелпист, Иеракс, Пеон, Валериан, Иуст и мученица Харита», which includes «Иуст» — Justus — whom the day line does not print and for whom no name link stands on this day. `justus-1-june` therefore took NO russian row in this batch, and the omission is a reading reported to the author rather than a decision. The passion as this source tells it: the eight were brought to Rome, imprisoned, and before the prefect Рустик confessed Christ; refusing to sacrifice they were sentenced and beheaded. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 1 iunie — «Sfântul Iustin Martirul și Filosoful»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 1ης Ιουνίου — «Άγιος Ιουστίνος ο Απολογητής και φιλόσοφος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 1 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps him, and it is the same man: the apologist of Flavia Neapolis who gave his apology to Antoninus Pius. **He is not the Justin the same day page keeps in the company of eight**, whom the corpus holds as `justin-companion-of-chariton`; the page prints the two as separate entries and its company page says they suffered together, «μαζί με τον φιλόσοφο και απολογητή Ιουστίνο (βλέπε ίδια ημέρα)». `dates` are added where the folder had none. **The page contradicts itself about the manner of his death** and both readings are quoted: its distich says hemlock took him from life, «Ἰουστῖνον κώνειον ἦρεν ἐκ βίου», while its prose says he was beheaded, «αποκεφαλίστηκε το 165 μ.X.» Two hymns are stored, the apolytikion and the kontakion, both of which name him; the megalynarion is left in the source.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 14.06.2026 (1. јун ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Јустин Философ“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, a line above the company and a different man. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. THE TWO Јустинс OF THIS DAY AND THE THIRD THE DAY LIST OFFERS. The Prologue prints Јустин twice on the Julian 1 June — once as the philosopher of this entry and once as the first name of the company below — and TWO COMMEMORATIONS ON ONE CALENDAR MEANS TWO MEN, which is also how doxologia and saint.gr keep them. The entries are told apart by everything: this one is a Samaritan-born Greek philosopher poisoned in a Roman prison, that one is a company of eight beheaded under the eparch Rusticus, and this book puts the two deaths three years apart, 166 against 163. AND THE DAY LIST’S THIRD OFFER IS REFUSED: `justin-popovich` is on the menologion 1/6 with a `greek venerated` row and an `undocumented serbian` one, and HE IS NOT THIS MAN — he is the archimandrite of Ćelije born 1894 and dead 1979, whom a Prologue of the 1920s cannot name. His `serbian` row is left `undocumented`. Taking the day list’s offer there would have put an ancient Alexandrian-school apologist’s life onto a twentieth-century Serbian theologian, which is the worst failure this job has. A BIRTH WIDENED BY FIVE YEARS AND A DEATH BY ONE. The folder held `birth` 100 off saint.gr («γεννήθηκε … το 100 μ.X.» and the heading’s «(100 - 165)») and `death` 165. This book states „105. године по Христу“ for the birth and „пресели се у блажену вечност 166. године“ for the death. Both are stated flat, so both are WIDENED and neither is chosen: `birth` 100 to 105, display «100 or 105»; `death` 165 to 166, display «165 or 166». The existing note’s own open question is answered one way by this book: saint.gr’s prose has him beheaded and its distich has hemlock take him, and THE PROLOGUE AGREES WITH THE DISTICH AND WITH DOXOLOGIA — Crescens poisons him in prison — so two books of three give poison and the manner is no longer one page’s oddity. The folder still records no manner, only the years. TWO MARTYRS HE SAW DIE GET NO ROW, NO FOLDER AND NO NAME IN THE PROSE. The entry says he was present at the martyrdom of two named Christians; the corpus keeps neither, `ls saints | grep -iE 'ptolem|luci'` returns only place-names and other men, and by the coordinator’s third ruling nothing is minted. Both names are in this note and in the commit message and in neither life. The emperors Antoninus and Marcus Aurelius get no row and are used for no year; Crescens the Cynic is already in the prose unlinked off doxologia and gains nothing — six folders share that forename, so the page’s own index poisons the form and no row is owed. `types` untouched: `martyr` and `apologist` are both corroborated, the second by the two apologies this entry counts. No `office`, no `locations`. THE EIGHT ONE-WAY `related` ROWS ON THIS FOLDER ARE LEFT FOR THE AUTHOR, AND THIS BOOK IS WHY. All eight of the company carry `justin-the-philosopher` in their `related`, on saint.gr’s «ελαβαν … μαζί» — they received the crowns together with him — and this folder’s own `related` is empty, so the reader cannot walk back. It was NOT completed here: the Prologue keeps the two as separate entries, narrates no shared martyrdom, and dates the two deaths three years apart, so its own numbers do not corroborate the «together» those eight rows rest on. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nestricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Mucenic Iustin Martirul și Filosoful, altui Mucenic Iustin și celor împreună cu dânșii; the site prints one hymn, the common of several martyrs, for both Justins and their companions.

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their contests received the crowns of incorruption from Thee our God; for having Thy strength they overcame the tormentors and broke the feeble insolence of the demons. At their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Φιλοσοφίας ταὶς ἀκτίσιν ἐκλάμπων, θεογνωσίας ὑποφήτης ἐδείχθης, σαφῶς παραταξάμενος κατὰ τῶν δυσμενῶν σὺ γὰρ ὠμολόγησας, ἀληθείας τὴν γνῶσιν, καὶ Μαρτύρων σύσκηνος, δι' ἀθλήσεως ὤφθης, μεθ' ὧν δυσώπει πάντοτε Χριστόν, ὢ Ἰουστίνε, ὑπὲρ τῶν ψυχῶν ἠμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος δ’, Ὁ ὑψωθεῖς ἐν τῷ Σταυρῷ, on the page of «Άγιος Ιουστίνος ο Απολογητής και φιλόσοφος»

english.text: Shining with the rays of philosophy, thou wast shown to be an interpreter of the knowledge of God, drawing up thy ranks plainly against the adversaries; for thou didst confess the knowledge of the truth, and by thy contest wast seen to share the tabernacle of the martyrs. With them entreat Christ always, O Justin, on behalf of our souls.

hymns.text: Τον αληθή, της ευσεβείας κήρυκα, και ευκλεή, των μυστηρίων ρήτορα, Ιουστίνον τον φιλόσοφον, μετ' εγκωμίων ευφημήσωμεν δυνάμει γαρ σοφίας τε και χάριτος, τον λόγον κατετράνωσε της πίστεως, αιτούμενος πάσι θείαν άφεσιν.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ήχος β', Τους ασφαλείς, on the page of «Άγιος Ιουστίνος ο Απολογητής και φιλόσοφος»

english.text: Let us praise with encomia the true herald of godliness and the glorious orator of the mysteries, Justin the philosopher; for by the power of wisdom and of grace he made plain the word of the faith, asking divine forgiveness for all.

hymns.text: Мученицы Твои, Господи,/ во страданиих своих венцы прияша нетленныя от Тебе, Бога нашего:/ имуще бо крепость Твою,/ мучителей низложиша,/ сокрушиша и демонов немощныя дерзости./ Тех молитвами// спаси души наша.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, «Тропарь мученика Иустина Философа и иже с ним», глас 4, under «Молитвы» on the day page for 1 июня ст. ст. It is the common of martyrs, printed in the plural and under no personal name, and its heading sets it over Justin the Philosopher and those with him — so it is the service of the whole company this day's first line enumerates, and it is copied whole here (BRIEF.md §4).

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings have received imperishable crowns from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength they cast down the tormentors and shattered the feeble insolence of the demons. By their prayers save our souls.

hymns.text: Премудростию Божественных твоих словес, Иустине,/ Церковь Божия вся украсившися,/ жития твоего светлостию мир освещает,/ излияния же ради крове венец прием/ и со Ангелы предстоя Христу,// моли непрестанно о всех нас.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, «Кондак мученика Иустина Философа», глас 2, under «Молитвы» on the day page for 1 июня ст. ст. It names him in the vocative and stands under his name alone, so it is on this folder only and not on the other seven of the company.

english.text: Adorned throughout by the wisdom of thy divine words, O Justin, the Church of God enlightens the world with the brightness of thy life; and having received a crown for the pouring out of thy blood, and standing with the angels before Christ, pray thou unceasingly for us all.

birth.note: saint.gr: «Ο Άγιος Ιουστίνος γεννήθηκε στη Φλαβία Νεάπολη της Παλαιστίνης το 100 μ.X. αι.» The page's heading repeats it, «Άγιος Ιουστίνος ο Απολογητής και φιλόσοφος (100 - 165)». The Охридски пролог for 1. јун ст. ст. gives a different year flat — „Рођен од јелинских родитеља у самаријском граду Сихему, доцније названом Наблус, 105. године по Христу“ — so the interval is widened to hold both and neither is chosen (5 October 2026).

death.note: saint.gr: «ο μέγας φιλόσοφος και ευσεβής χριστιανός συνελήφθη και αφού υπέστη διάφορα βασανιστήρια, αποκεφαλίστηκε το 165 μ.X.» The Охридски пролог for 1. јун ст. ст. gives one year later, flat: „Тако сконча свој земни живот овај велики заштитник вере хришћанске, и пресели се у блажену вечност 166. године“, so the interval is widened to hold both. The two books also disagree on the manner and this folder records none: saint.gr's prose has him beheaded, its own distich has hemlock take him, and both doxologia and the Prologue have Crescens the Cynic poison him in prison (5 October 2026).
